$comment: Fixed, reviewed golden fixtures for the secure-aggregation fixed-point encoding profile (Work Packages F, G, H, AL). Every 'encoded' value below was computed independently of the C++/Python implementation under test -- by hand, using plain round-half-away-from-zero arithmetic on value * scale_factor -- and is checked against the real implementation's output in cpp/coordinator/tests/fixed_point_encoding_test.cpp (C++) and (once written) python/tests/secure_aggregation/test_fixed_point_encoding.py (Python). Do not regenerate this file by running the implementation and capturing its output -- that would defeat the purpose of an independent fixture. Any change to these values requires re-deriving them by hand and re-reviewing, not re-running the code.

profile.scale_factor_note: 2^20 -- power of two, so value * scale_factor is exact in IEEE-754 double arithmetic for every value used below

encode_cases.note: 3.5 * 2^20 is an exact integer; no rounding actually occurs
IEEE-754 -0.0 == 0.0 and -0.0 * scale_factor == 0.0 (or -0.0, which casts to integer 0 either way); no special-case branch needed in the implementation
value is exactly 0.5 / scale_factor; a genuine round-half case, not a floating-point-imprecision artifact, since scale_factor is a power of two
1/3 -- rounds down since the fractional part (.333) is below .5
exactly at max_input_magnitude -- inclusive boundary, must be accepted

domain_bounds_case.note: 1048576010000000256 < 9223372036854775807 (2^63 - 1), with roughly 3 more orders of magnitude of headroom -- comfortably safe without needing 128-bit intermediate arithmetic, as analyzed in docs/fixed-point-secure-encoding.md
